literal: Many factions, ruin-causing internal enmity, and ruler-harassing destructive rebellious chieftains, that which is without is a country.
translation: A true country is one that is free from warring factions, ruinous internal enmities, and murderous, rebellious chieftains who harass the ruler.
modern: பல பிரிவுகளாகப் பிரிந்து சண்டையிடும் குழுக்களும், நாட்டைப் பாழாக்கும் உட்பகையும், அரசனைத் துன்புறுத்தும் கொலைத்தொழில் புரியும் குறும்நில மன்னர்களும் இல்லாததே சிறந்த நாடாகும்.
explanation: This couplet defines a stable nation by identifying three internal threats it must be free from. First, 'palkuḻu' refers to multiple conflicting factions or sects that divide the populace. Second, 'uṭpakai' represents treasonous internal enmity that quietly ruins the state from within. Third, 'koṟumpu' refers to rebellious, lawless chieftains or marauders who harass the sovereign ruler and disrupt governance. A prosperous and secure country is one that remains entirely free from these three destructive forces.
